_comment: Replayable payloads rolled up from tests/live/runs/tm/*.json by the capability-live-probe orchestrator. Phase 2 COMPLETE: all 69 capabilities probed across 7 batches. Only capabilities whose probe returned a 2xx appear in "payloads". Replaying depends on the live fixture - run `npm run seed:live` first, and note that many arguments reference objects created during probe runs (see each run file's setup[]). WARNING: a 2xx from a tm write does NOT reliably mean the write took effect - see findings/test-run-writes-untrustworthy-systemic.md. A replay checker must verify against storage, not against the response.
phase: phase 1 + phase 2; payloads rolled up from tests/live/runs/tm/*.json

clone_exploratory_session_v1.replay_note: flat body, no exploratory_session wrapper. This exercises only the SYNC path (source had 2 logs, well under the 50-log threshold) - the async path (>=50 logs, 202, no session object returned) is untested and structurally different. The clone's own inline response under-reports session_log_count/timeline immediately after a sync clone even though the logs were genuinely copied (confirmed by a follow-up read) - see findings/clone_exploratory_session_v1.md.

close_test_run_v1.replay_note: No body at all - the transition to run_state:closed is fixed. This run is now permanently closed on preprod (a real state change, not a scratch object), so do not replay this exact call again. The write's own 200 misreports two of its own fields: uuid comes back as 359844 instead of the run's real uuid 17578623, and closed_by comes back null even though the run was genuinely closed by a real user (both confirmed wrong via an immediate get_test_run_by_integer_id_v1 read-back). project_id is returned as an integer though the schema declares it a string. type, self_ui_link and observability_url are declared on testrun and never returned; attachments, created_by and updated_by are returned but undeclared. See findings/close_test_run_v1.md.

create_folder_v2.replay_note: name carries a {{unique}} placeholder: a fixed folder name makes every replay after the first a 400 'Folder with same name exists', and the failure body's `message` then reads as an undeclared success field

create_report_v2.replay_note: title carries {{unique}}: a fixed report title collides on replay and 400s, and the error body's fields then read as undeclared successes

create_shared_step_v1.replay_note: folder_id must be a shared-field/shared-step folder id, NOT a test-case folder id - they are separate id namespaces. Omitting folder_id leaves the step at folder root (Unassigned), which is what worked here. The pool's __scratch__ folder (764138) is a test-case folder and 400s with 'Target folder not found' if passed as folder_id.
